title: The Twelfth Language
summary: Bram's spectacles can read the twelfth language. Barely. It is a Rift-native notation system that predates human contact with the Ember Rift by centuries. There are forty-three glyphs in the Architect's Verge. Reading them all produces something that might be instructions, a warning, or a map of what was supposed to happen.

phases.label: Document all 43 glyphs in the Architect's Verge

onComplete.text: Forty-three glyphs. Bram's notes fill two journals. The language is not a human adaptation of something alien — it is the original, partially translated by someone who knew both systems. 'Someone was translating in both directions,' Bram says. 'This was a correspondence.'

phases.label: Complete Bram's translation of the glyph sequence

onComplete.text: The translation is not instructions or a warning. It is a record of the original negotiation: the first time a human entered the Rift willingly and came back, sixty years before the Brightfall Council's founding. The negotiator's name is in the first glyph. It is also on a portrait in the Brightfall Council chamber.

phases.label: Apply the glyph knowledge to the final confrontation

onComplete.text: The glyph knowledge changes the final confrontation — specifically, it changes what the party can say and what the Sovereign understands them to mean. The original negotiation ended badly. This one does not have to.
